claim: legacy MET2/MET3 entity ages are read as milliseconds and converted, while MET4 stores server ticks, so a pre-20TPS save no longer despawns all its drops
regression_fixed: the 20TPS cutover made one tick 50ms, so a legacy 300000 ms age read as 300000 ticks exceeded the 6000 tick life and removed every saved drop on the first tick. I introduced this in the cutover commit.
format: magic MET3 -> MET4. MET4 ages are server ticks. MET2/MET3 ages are milliseconds divided by TICK_MS.
negative_controls: all 3 detected: legacy ages read as ticks (the pre-fix bug), MET4 ages wrongly converted from ms, millisecond divisor using ticks per second
implementation_error: expected value was written as 150, which is the 4TPS result of 3000/20; the correct value at 50 ms per tick is 60. The test caught it.
tests: 31 passed, 0 failed, 1 explicitly ignored, serial and at 8 threads
review: NOT RUN, external usage limit still in force for eight consecutive slices
provenance_note: the cutover-20tps results.json records a hash for src/furnace_cache_tests.rs that predates a trailing-whitespace fix made after that measurement. The committed file matches HEAD and HEAD~1. The difference is whitespace only, so the cutover measurement remains valid, but that receipt hash is stale.
